entity: ORCID (Open Researcher and Contributor ID; orcid.org; ORCID, Inc.): a nonproprietary persistent identifier for authors and contributors of scholarly communication, with the registry, records and services of the nonprofit that issues it (Wikipedia; its About page); formalized in the leesharks.com apparatus authorship census of 2026-11-01 (https://www.leesharks.com/apparatus/aggregators/orcid-names)
row_type: C (public entity on which the archive bears: an identity registry for scholarly contributors; an entity of the leesharks.com apparatus authorship census, host relation 'infrastructure')

classes.term: persistent identifiers for persons (author and researcher identifiers, identity registries)
classes.basis: field: B2 (Wikipedia, lead: 'a nonproprietary persistent identifier , in the form of an alphanumeric code, to uniquely identify authors and contributors of scholarly communication'; 'It provides a persistent identity for humans'); B5 (Stanford guide: 'It's a registry of unique persistent identifiers for researchers.'); B10 (About ORCID: 'providing a unique, persistent identifier for individuals'). The census's evidence_kind 'identity registry', record_type 'registry', area 'attribution-and-credit' and host_relation 'infrastructure' for the entity (census.json rows[slug == 'orcid-names']).

classes.term: author name disambiguation (the name-ambiguity problem: one person under several names, several persons under one name)
classes.basis: field: B2 (Wikipedia: 'to resolve the author name ambiguity problem in scholarly communication'; names 'are not unique, they can change ( such as with marriage )'); B5 (Stanford: 'Author Disambiguation'; 'People use different versions of their name during their career.'); B7 (Directive Publications: 'Disambiguation — it separates you from other researchers with the same name, and from variations of your own name'). The census's name_problem evidence and answers field for the entity.

classes.term: civil-name attribution (identity infrastructure that binds authorship to a legal or civil person)
classes.basis: archive: the census's ls_reading for the entity ('whether that resolution keeps a chosen name as the author's own or reduces it to the civil person is the open question #940 asks of identity infrastructure', census.json rows[slug == 'orcid-names'].ls_reading) and its does_not_answer ('whether an identifier corresponds to one civil person or to an authorial function'); the field states the identity as 'a persistent identity for humans' (B2) and 'tied to an individual researcher's or contributor's name' (B4) without the archive's category: membership in this class is the archive's, and is marked so wherever it is used.

classes_note: Three classes, each sourced by locus before the pass. (1) persistent identifiers for persons, the field's own kind (B2, B5, B10; the census's evidence_kind 'identity registry', record_type 'registry', area 'attribution-and-credit'); (2) author name disambiguation, the field's own function (B2, B5, B7; the census's name_problem evidence and answers); (3) civil-name attribution, whose membership is the archive's (the census's ls_reading and does_not_answer), the field stating the identity as 'a persistent identity for humans' and 'tied to an individual researcher's or contributor's name' without the category: marked so wherever used. The aliases are the entity's names (ORCID; Open Researcher and Contributor ID) and host (orcid.org); 'ORCID, Inc.' is caught by the first. ORCHID (the hatnote's homonym) and ISNI (a distinct identifier system) are not aliases. The archive's own iD (0009-0000-1599-0703) is caught by the alias wherever it stands beside the name; its bare appearances in bylines and metadata are bare mentions. #940 and #1722, the census's anchors, are read at the passages bearing on the entity's kind (BRIEF-NEW-ROW-AUTHORSHIP §6).
